extracted.intended_audience: Fortune readers and general public interested in business, advertising, and corporate controversy
extracted.subtask_description: A short news article reporting on a controversial advertising campaign (an Audi commercial aired in China) and the public and regulatory reactions to it. Covers the ad content, audience backlash, company response, and a related past incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sexist or objectifying content
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers in China are not happy with Audi’s new advertisement that compares women to used cars. The ad immediately sparked controversy on Weibo... with people calling Audi’s ad sexist. Some people called it “unacceptable” and “disgusting” while others vowed to boycott the German automaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article illustrates the anti-pattern (an ad that equates a bride to a used car, with scenes of inspection of the bride’s body). Public reaction on social platforms can be severe (calls of 'sexist', boycott threats). Ads should not objectify or dehumanize people; anticipate and avoid imagery or metaphors that liken people to products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not promote reckless or unsafe behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: This isn’t the first time an Audi ad has gone wrong. Last August, Audi pulled an ad in the United Kingdom after the Advertising Standards Authority (ASA)... said it promoted reckless driving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators such as the ASA will judge ads that appear to promote unsafe behavior. Avoid imagery or messaging that glorifies or normalizes reckless driving or other dangerous acts; legal/regulatory complaints can force removals and reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align advertising with stated company values
rubrics_metrics.description: An Audi spokesperson said: 'The ad’s perception that has been created for many people does not correspond to the values of our company in any way.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brands should ensure campaigns reflect corporate values and brand promises. If an ad’s public perception conflicts with company values, it creates reputational risk and may require corrective action or public statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly to public backlash: remove content and investigate
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi has since pulled the ad — produced by FAW-Volkswagen — and said it is currently conducting a 'thorough investigation' to ensure that similar incidents don't happen again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended corporate response to high-profile backlash includes removing the offending content, issuing statements, and investigating how the ad was produced/approved to prevent recurrence. Swift, transparent action can mitigate further damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider local cultural sensitivities and monitor social platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: The commercial, which recently aired in China... immediately sparked controversy on Weibo, China’s Twitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ads that may be acceptable in one market can be offensive in another. Local cultural norms and the dynamics of local social platforms (e.g., Weibo) should be tested and monitored; pre-release local review and monitoring after release are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use certification/assurance messaging to reassure buyers (in used-car ads)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final sequence of the ad includes a screen grab of used Audis for sale, with the narrator saying, 'Only with official certification can you be rest assured.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When marketing used vehicles, highlighting official certification can be an effective reassurance to buyers. However, such messaging should be paired with ethical, non-offensive creative execution to avoid undermining the reassurance.
